data.completion_memo: Implemented execution-v1 standing permission identity for native Shell/Python host/start tools, excluding only descriptions/instructions. Complete invocation/replay identity remains untouched. Transactional migration requires an extant valid project-tool grant, same project key and exact historical frozen binding hash; it never creates permission from reviews/receipts and leaves unprovable formats unmatched. Migration scan memoization avoids repeating unchanged history scans. Audit verified authority fields remain hashed, cross-project evidence rejected, exact old binding evidence required, metadata-only changes compatible, executable/config/schema/limits/approval changes incompatible, idempotence and durable revocation. Desktop suite 357 passed/1 ignored. Native isolated app created two user grants, downgraded them to legacy exact-binding hashes, changed current instructions, restarted, and executed real Shell and Python with zero reviewer calls. Revoking both grants restored two automatic reviews. Evidence: desktop/src-tauri/target/native-approval-cache-1789732599799/proof.json and verified.png. User runtime data, settings, and grants were not directly altered by verification; migration will run when the rebuilt application starts.
data.description: Third implementation step. Version execution-relevant permission identity; descriptions/instructions do not invalidate grants. Recover extant compatible grants using trusted stored binding evidence; preserve revocation, project isolation and fail-closed behavior on authority changes. Native upgrade proof must show zero reviewer calls for existing compatible grants. Design: docs/approval-cache-accounting.md.
data.title: Reuse compatible saved project permissions across tool updates
